messages:
jamal: quick check — noticed a short spike of 502s hitting /v1/generate at ~10:30 UTC in prod. small but visible on the per-route error heatmap, any pointers where to grab traces + root-cause quickly?
sophia: start with the 'prod/request-errors' dashboard — filter by route=/v1/generate and status=502. dash link: https://grafana.redwood/services/d/prod-request-errors ???panel=errors
eng-observability-bot: automated alert triggered: PROD_ROUTE_502_RATE (10:30 UTC) — rate: 0.6% (baseline 0.05%). Logs pushed to Kibana: https://logs.redwood/prod/_search?q=request.path:%22/v1/generate%22%20AND%20status:502
alex: for traces use Jaeger: https://jaeger.redwood/search?service=api&operation=Generate&minDuration=0ms&tags=%7B%22http.status_code%22:%22502%22%7D — pull a few spans around 10:28-10:34 UTC. also look for upstream:gateway or lb timeouts.
maria: quick grep if you prefer CLI:
```
aws logs filter-log-events --log-group-name "/prod/api" --start-time 1700000000000 --end-time 1700000200000 --filter-pattern '"/v1/generate" "502"' | jq -r '.events[].message' | head
```
(that start/end are example ms — convert the time window to your incident)
jamal: thanks — any common config we should check? proxy timeouts, kvcache eviction, or batching overload?
sophia: check gateway -> backend timeout mismatch first. There was a recent batching bump on dedicated nodes last deploy (PR #4123). If backend slower during large prompt sizes, gateway may 502 on timeout.
eng-observability-bot: note: recent deploy 2233280000 rolled batching=16 default for model-x on dedicated pool-alpha.
alex: also look at the request payload sizes + attention length. if KV cache miss storm happens we see CPU/GPU stalls then upstreams return 502. Metrics: gpu-util, model-latency, kvcache-miss-rate on the per-pool dash.
maria: action for triage: 1) grab 3 sample request-ids from logs 2) run Jaeger trace lookup 3) check dedicated pool CPU/GPU and queue length around spike 4) check gateway logs for 502 reason (upstream timeout vs connection reset).
jamal: grabbed two request ids: rq_8a3f and rq_8a41. pasted one sample log line: 2025-06-12T10:30:12.345Z [info] request_id=rq_8a3f route=/v1/generate status=502 upstream_reason="504 gateway timeout" latency_ms=6200 prompt_len=2300
kate: seems like gateway upstream timeout. For alerts: we should avoid firing on short blips. propose debouncing PROD_ROUTE_502_RATE from 2m->8m and add per-route scope for /v1/generate so global noise doesn't show. Also add exclude for health and metrics endpoints.
sophia: sounds reasonable. Another tweak: change threshold from 0.5%->0.8% for short windows, but keep an SLA alert that monitors 30m window >0.3%.
amor (maria): pinging on the PR to change alerting rules, I'll open a small PR to: exclude /healthz, add per-route filter, set evaluation window 8m, threshold 0.8%. assigning to @kate for review.
maria: PR opened -> https://git.redwood/infra/alerts/pulls/78 — @kate can you review when you have a sec?
kate: on it, will review in ~30m. if this looks like a rollout regresssion we should also add a temporary rollback/rollback-guard in the deploy runbook.
jamal: thanks everyone — quick note for follow-ups: i'll attach sample traces in the PR and tag the model team if we need to revert batching. low priority for oncall unless spike persists. :thumbsup:
